claims.text: The proposed alloy is equiatomic Ti–Nb–Ta–Mo–W.
Superconductivity in equiatomic Ti–Nb–Ta–Mo–W is governed predominantly by the degree of local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions modulate the phonon spectrum.
Changes in the phonon spectrum modify the electron–phonon coupling responsible for superconducting pairing.
Arc melting followed by rapid quenching ensures a single-phase Ti–Nb–Ta–Mo–W solid solution.
The as-quenched alloy has moderate inherent lattice distortions.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation, such as high-pressure torsion, enhances local lattice distortions in the alloy.
Annealing at 900°C for 100 hours relieves local lattice distortions in the alloy.
Strain-induced variations in interatomic distances alter the phonon spectrum.
Enhanced local lattice distortions broaden phonon modes.
Phonon-mode broadening modifies electron–phonon coupling strength.
Increased disorder may suppress Tc through pair breaking.
Under some conditions, increased disorder may enhance Tc by strengthening electron–phonon coupling.
SPD-treated samples will exhibit broader phonon linewidths than annealed samples.
SPD-treated samples will exhibit a shift in Tc relative to annealed samples, although the direction of the shift is unspecified.
A correlation between phonon broadening and the magnitude or sign of the Tc shift would support the proposed mechanism.
The proposed interpretation applies only when the alloy remains single-phase and lattice distortion can be varied without major compositional changes or phase separation.
A measurable change in the phonon spectrum without a systematic and reproducible Tc shift would falsify the claim that local lattice distortions govern superconductivity in this alloy.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as the as-quenched material, but the predicted outcome and falsification rule describe the annealed, strain-relieved material as the baseline. This makes the intended controlled reference ambiguous.
